title: Contour model
description: A Contour specification in the framework's structured-record style (Section 3) with a nested ownership hierarchy: Components nest under their System (groups), and the elements a Component owns — functions, dataObjects, events — nest under that Component. A Component's contracts (Section 3.3) are keyed by the Actor they serve, or by the reserved key `Components`. Actors are top-level (they sit outside the Component boundary). Requirement and Guardrail definitions (Section 3.6) are top-level and referenced by name. Ownership is expressed by nesting; cross-boundary edges (groups, uses, consumes, references, dependsOn) and Function steps are inline by name. No IDs. Field names are camelCase.

System.description: The business-capability grouping and root of the ownership tree. A model has at most one System in this style; given as a single element or a one-item list.

Actor.description: An external role with distinct access to the Components it uses (Section 3). Top-level because it sits outside the Component boundary. Which Components it uses is derived from the contracts keyed by its name. Given as a single element or a list.

Requirement.description: Record-tier Requirement definitions (Section 3.6), referenced by name from the requirements list of the elements they apply to.

Guardrail.description: Record-tier Guardrail definitions (Section 3.6), referenced by name from the guardrails list of the elements they bound.

name.description: Plain-language element name (Section 3.5); the stable identifier other elements reference by.

description.description: Required plain-language sentence or two — what this element is (Section 3.3).

nameList.description: A list of element or definition names referenced inline.

requirements.description: Names of Requirement definitions this element must satisfy (Section 3.6).

guardrails.description: Names of Guardrail definitions this element must stay inside (Section 3.6).

schemaField.description: The structured shape of a Data Object or Event (Section 3.3): an inline mapping of field names to types in the core type notation — primitives, enum(...), T[], T[1..], T?, references to Data Objects, and nested types — or a string link to an existing spec (AsyncAPI/JSON Schema/Avro) rather than a re-authored duplicate.

firstStep.description: The first entry of a Function's steps list. Besides the ordinary step verbs it may be `consumes`, naming an Event produced by another Component — marking the Function as subscribed to that Event (Sections 3.3, 3.4).

step.description: One entry of a Function's ordered steps list (Section 3.3): a single-key mapping of a step verb to the name of the element it acts on. `consumes` is allowed only as the first step (see `firstStep`).

contractKey.description: A contract key: the name of an Actor, or the reserved key `Components` for Functions of other Components (Section 3.3). That an Actor name refers to an existing Actor is checked outside JSON Schema.

style.description: The style whose binding interprets every other key in this block (e.g. OpenAPI, gRPC, AsyncAPI).

binding.description: The contract's technical side (Section 3.3). Contour defines only `style`; every other key is defined by that style's binding, outside the paper.

contract.description: The access a Component offers to one kind of caller (Section 3.3).

callers.description: Keys of the Component contracts this Function is reached through: Actor names, or `Components` (Section 3.3).

operation.description: The operation, once per style among the callers' contract bindings, keyed by `binding.style`. Each value is in that style's own format — e.g. an OpenAPI path and Operation Object, or a gRPC rpc definition — and is validated by the style's binding, not by this schema.

functionContract.description: An external Function's contract (Section 3.3): who may call it, and the operation they call.

groups.description: The Components this System groups, nested as full element objects (ownership by nesting).

contract.description: The access this Component offers, keyed by who it is for: an Actor's name, or `Components` (Section 3.3). Keying makes 'one contract per caller' structural. That each key names an existing Actor is checked outside JSON Schema.

functions.description: The Functions this Component performs, nested (ownership by nesting).

dataObjects.description: The Data Objects this Component owns, nested.

events.description: The Events this Component produces, nested. An Event this Component only reacts to is referenced by name via `consumes`, not nested (it is owned by the producing Component).

references.description: Names of Data Objects owned by another Component that this Component reads/references (Context-view resolution).

consumes.description: Names of Events produced by another Component that this Component reacts to — a Context-view summary of its Functions' `consumes` first steps (Section 3.4).

dependsOn.description: Names of Components this Component depends on — a Context-view summary of its Functions' `uses` steps (Section 3.2).

behavior.description: Prose account of business rules and side effects, precise enough that its logic isn't left for an LLM to invent (Section 3.3).

steps.description: Ordered list of the Function's own edges — `consumes` (first step only), calls, uses, reads, modifies, produces — the authoritative sequence the diagram's edges summarize (Section 3.3). A `uses` step never names a contract: the caller determines it.

function.description: A Function (Section 3). External when it declares a `contract`; private otherwise. Functions have no `schema`. A Function started by an Event (`consumes` first step) has no contract (check 5).

name.description: Event name, in the past tense (Section 3.5), e.g. "Order Placed".

definition.description: A record-tier Requirement or Guardrail definition (Section 3.6): a name and a description, referenced by name from the elements it applies to. Never drawn as a diagram element.
